entries.closedGap: Installed TDLib error/rejection producer and recovery classification
evidence: tdl8.1.0 Client._handleReceive wraps unsolicited error objects in TDLibError; handleReceive emits the native Error, wrapping non-Error or cross-realm thrown values in local UnknownError. Actual installed prototype methods exercised without native client startup.

Request error replies reject pending calls with TDLibError; three restriction codes remain recognized by existing tests. Client._handleClose rejects with same-realm new Error(Client was closed), satisfying current expected-close suppression.

The client.on(error) diagnostic callback still reads err.message||err; it was not changed into a restrictive instance check. The relevant change is process unhandled-rejection expected-close suppression and diagnostic/restriction helpers.

Native Errors preserve identity; cross-realm/plain thrown values normalized by TDLib already lacked their arbitrary message in the old outward UnknownError. Arbitrary application-created plain objects no longer impersonate restricted-content or expected-close errors. This is intentional stricter classification, not an SDK producer regression.

Current valid provider/native/system errors remain supported. No blanket equivalence is asserted for externally fabricated unhandled rejection objects with a message property or cross-realm Error injected directly into process handlers. Such values now fail closed instead of silently suppressing fatal recovery.

entries.closedGap: Trailing-digit XML contract grammar and one shared pattern deadline
evidence: Receipt-origin signal_contract PATH_PATTERN already permits trailing digits in every lowercase path segment, including nested paths. Parser previously rejected those otherwise valid configured tags; current grammar aligns parser with unchanged contract validator.

Actual validateSignalContractDefinition and validateSignalXml probes accept note1, note_0 and group1.note2; invalid leading digit/underscore, hyphen, uppercase and empty path segment remain rejected by contract validation. Unapproved numbered tags and malformed/mismatched XML remain rejected.

Existing complete contract test executes30ordinary individually cheap field regexes successfully; substituting a monotonically advancing clock across fields then rejects within shared budget. One deadline is created before additionalFields iteration; remaining timeout is derived per field, never reset to100.

Existing bounded subprocess fixtures reject three catastrophic patterns with a5second outer timeout; cheap Unicode/escaped/grouped patterns retain semantics. Additional allowed-value/length checks precede pattern matching and geometry checks still follow field validation.

The100ms value is an aggregate field-pattern execution budget with elapsed/setup overhead; it does not claim a hard100ms wall bound for the entire signal parser or unrestricted concurrent requests. Limiting formerly unbounded regex execution intentionally rejects excessive work.
limits: Grammar expansion repairs mismatch with existing authorable contract, not permission for arbitrary tags.
Shared-budget clock test is deterministic policy evidence; subprocess tests additionally exercise real vm timeout. No global CPU/rate-limit guarantee is inferred.
